REC_J01.text: Java supports object-oriented principles including encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.

REC_J02.text: Java classes can implement multiple interfaces but can extend only one abstract superclass.

REC_J03.text: Method overriding allows a subclass in Java to define a specialized version of an inherited method.

REC_J04.text: Java garbage collector automatically deallocates heap memory occupied by unreferenced objects.

REC_J05.text: Abstract classes in Java cannot be directly instantiated and define common contracts for derived subclasses.

REC_J06.text: Java Generics provide compile-time type safety by allowing classes and methods to operate on parameterized types.

REC_M01.text: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors characterize invariant directional vectors under linear matrix transformations.

REC_M02.text: Singular Value Decomposition factors any real matrix into left-singular, singular values, and right-singular matrices.

REC_M03.text: The inner dot product computes vector projection and normalizes to cosine similarity in metric spaces.

REC_M04.text: Matrix multiplication distributes over addition and is associative but strictly non-commutative in general.

REC_M05.text: Principal Component Analysis projects high-dimensional data onto orthogonal axes maximizing variance.

REC_M06.text: Matrix determinants quantify the scaling factor of the transformation on volume spanned by column vectors.

REC_V01.text: FAISS provides fast approximate nearest neighbor search using inverted file index and product quantization.

REC_V02.text: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs offer logarithmic time complexity for vector similarity retrieval.

REC_V03.text: Cosine distance and Euclidean L2 distance are standard distance metrics for comparing dense vector embeddings.

REC_V04.text: Vector databases index high-dimensional embeddings generated by transformer models for semantic search.

REC_V05.text: Inverted file index with flat quantization partitions vector space into Voronoi cells to accelerate search.

REC_V06.text: Dense vector retrieval systems utilize approximate nearest neighbors algorithms to compare query embeddings against documents.

REC_V07.text: HNSW index structures enable scalable semantic search across millions of dense embedding vectors in sub-linear time.

REC_V08.text: Product Quantization compresses dense vector representations to reduce memory usage in large-scale vector search engines.

REC_V09.text: Dense vector retrieval compares high-dimensional semantic vectors using cosine similarity distance thresholds.

REC_V10.text: Vector similarity search engines query dense embedding vectors generated by encoder neural models.

REC_P01.text: NumPy provides ndarray objects for efficient vector and matrix computations in Python.

REC_P02.text: Pandas DataFrames support tabular data manipulation, filtering, aggregation, and time-series operations.

REC_P03.text: Polars is an ultra-fast columnar DataFrame library implemented in Rust with a Python API.

REC_P04.text: Vectorized operations in NumPy eliminate explicit Python loops for substantial performance acceleration.

REC_P05.text: Python classes support object-oriented programming with multiple inheritance, method overriding, and dynamic polymorphism.

REC_P06.text: Python abstract base classes define blueprint interface contracts and enforce abstract method implementations on subclasses.

REC_ML01.text: PyTorch tensors support automatic differentiation via autograd for gradient-based neural network optimization.

REC_ML02.text: Cross-entropy loss measures the discrepancy between predicted probability distributions and true categorical labels.

REC_ML03.text: Adam optimizer dynamically adapts learning rates using first and second momentum estimates of gradients.

REC_ML04.text: DataLoaders in PyTorch handle batching, shuffling, and multi-threaded data prefetching for model training.

REC_ML05.text: Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss function with respect to model parameters via chain rule.

REC_ML06.text: Dropout regularization randomly deactivates neural connections during training to mitigate model overfitting.

REC_DB01.text: Relational databases enforce ACID guarantees: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

REC_DB02.text: B-Tree indexes provide logarithmic time lookups for equality and range queries in relational database tables.

REC_DB03.text: Database normalization organizes tables to minimize data redundancy and eliminate update anomalies.

REC_DB04.text: SQL JOIN operations combine rows from two or more tables based on a related common key column.

REC_DB05.text: Foreign key constraints preserve referential integrity between child and parent tables in SQL schemas.

REC_DB06.text: Write-Ahead Logging ensures database transactions can be recovered after power failures or crashes.

REC_DS01.text: The CAP theorem states a distributed data store can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.

REC_DS02.text: Raft consensus algorithm selects a leader to manage replicated state machines across distributed cluster nodes.

REC_DS03.text: Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when distributed cache nodes are dynamically added or removed.

REC_DS04.text: Two-Phase Commit coordinates atomic transactions across autonomous distributed database nodes.

REC_DS05.text: Gossip protocols disseminate membership state across large peer-to-peer networks with high fault tolerance.

REC_DS06.text: Vector clocks track causality and detect concurrent updates in distributed key-value storage systems.

REC_ML02.text: Cross-entropy loss measures the discrepancy between predicted probability distributions and true categorical labels.

REC_ML03.text: Adam optimizer dynamically adapts learning rates using first and second momentum estimates of gradients.

REC_ML04.text: DataLoaders in PyTorch handle batching, shuffling, and multi-threaded data prefetching for model training.

REC_ML05.text: Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss function with respect to model parameters via chain rule.

REC_ML06.text: Dropout regularization randomly deactivates neural connections during training to mitigate model overfitting.

REC_DB01.text: Relational databases enforce ACID guarantees: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

REC_DB02.text: B-Tree indexes provide logarithmic time lookups for equality and range queries in relational database tables.

REC_DB03.text: Database normalization organizes tables to minimize data redundancy and eliminate update anomalies.

REC_DB04.text: SQL JOIN operations combine rows from two or more tables based on a related common key column.

REC_DB05.text: Foreign key constraints preserve referential integrity between child and parent tables in SQL schemas.

REC_DB06.text: Write-Ahead Logging ensures database transactions can be recovered after power failures or crashes.

REC_DS01.text: The CAP theorem states a distributed data store can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.

REC_DS02.text: Raft consensus algorithm selects a leader to manage replicated state machines across distributed cluster nodes.

REC_DS03.text: Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when distributed cache nodes are dynamically added or removed.

REC_DS04.text: Two-Phase Commit coordinates atomic transactions across autonomous distributed database nodes.

REC_DS05.text: Gossip protocols disseminate membership state across large peer-to-peer networks with high fault tolerance.

REC_DS06.text: Vector clocks track causality and detect concurrent updates in distributed key-value storage systems.

REC_J01.text: Java supports object-oriented principles including encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.

REC_J02.text: Java classes can implement multiple interfaces but can extend only one abstract superclass.

REC_J03.text: Method overriding allows a subclass in Java to define a specialized version of an inherited method.

REC_J04.text: Java garbage collector automatically deallocates heap memory occupied by unreferenced objects.

REC_J05.text: Abstract classes in Java cannot be directly instantiated and define common contracts for derived subclasses.

REC_J06.text: Java Generics provide compile-time type safety by allowing classes and methods to operate on parameterized types.

REC_M01.text: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors characterize invariant directional vectors under linear matrix transformations.

REC_M02.text: Singular Value Decomposition factors any real matrix into left-singular, singular values, and right-singular matrices.

REC_M03.text: The inner dot product computes vector projection and normalizes to cosine similarity in metric spaces.

REC_M04.text: Matrix multiplication distributes over addition and is associative but strictly non-commutative in general.

REC_M05.text: Principal Component Analysis projects high-dimensional data onto orthogonal axes maximizing variance.

REC_M06.text: Matrix determinants quantify the scaling factor of the transformation on volume spanned by column vectors.

REC_V01.text: FAISS provides fast approximate nearest neighbor search using inverted file index and product quantization.

REC_V02.text: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs offer logarithmic time complexity for vector similarity retrieval.

REC_V03.text: Cosine distance and Euclidean L2 distance are standard distance metrics for comparing dense vector embeddings.

REC_V04.text: Vector databases index high-dimensional embeddings generated by transformer models for semantic search.

REC_V05.text: Inverted file index with flat quantization partitions vector space into Voronoi cells to accelerate search.

REC_V06.text: Dense vector retrieval systems utilize approximate nearest neighbors algorithms to compare query embeddings against documents.

REC_V07.text: HNSW index structures enable scalable semantic search across millions of dense embedding vectors in sub-linear time.

REC_V08.text: Product Quantization compresses dense vector representations to reduce memory usage in large-scale vector search engines.

REC_V09.text: Dense vector retrieval compares high-dimensional semantic vectors using cosine similarity distance thresholds.

REC_V10.text: Vector similarity search engines query dense embedding vectors generated by encoder neural models.
